title: Echo videos estimate CT-referenced coronary-calcium categories
summary: A video neural network estimated coronary-calcium categories from echocardiograms. In 92 patients from a separate hospital, AUC was 0.75 for zero calcium and 0.85 for high calcium. This retrospective clinical validation does not establish screening benefit or replacement of CT.
ai_technology: R2+1D convolutional neural network; EchoNet-Dynamic transfer learning
organization: University of California, San Francisco; Cedars-Sinai Medical Center; Stanford University

evidence.tested: Development used 2,881 echocardiograms from 1,635 patients, paired with CT calcium scores; the reported external set contained 92 patients.
evidence.unknown: Selected patients had both tests within one year. Internal splitting is described by echocardiograms rather than clearly separated patients; external results are represented separately. Preventive-treatment benefit and population-screening performance were not tested.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained spatiotemporal CNN learns echo-video features associated with CT-derived calcium labels.

source_review.scope: Exact primary front DOI/title/PMCID/date, indexed primary clinical/model Methods and Results, fresh primary publication-status metadata. Author PDF returned HTTP202 and was not read.
